correctness.rationale: For each pair of endpoint computational-basis strings, the exact physical average over independent CZ erasures and all accepted equal-sign X outcomes is an explicit 16-state replica transfer contraction with alternating parity projectors. Direct enumeration of all 256 two-layer erasure patterns independently reproduces the transfer matrix at four noise levels. At zero noise each parity-sector two-step matrix has rank one, isolated eigenvalue 64, and exactly computed perturbation coefficients -384 at first order and 1536/1280/1088 at second order. Taking eigenvalue ratios over n/2 layers gives the claimed exp(-2c) and exp(-7c/2) with controlled analytic remainders; the normalized boundary contributions are exact at p=0. The limiting state is Bell-diagonal in the graph basis, so its partial-transpose negativity and unique separability boundary follow algebraically. The heralding-probability law follows from the common -6p logarithmic eigenvalue coefficient, with the full acceptance normalization tracked. Finite experiments are corroboration, not substituted for the asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: Original double-rail graph architecture and edge-erasure postselection belong to Szymański–Vandré–Gühne (arXiv:2402.00937, 2024), whose quantitative statement is first-order, fixed-length susceptibility and isolated-edge correction. The current claim is a noncommuting weak-noise/large-length scaling theorem giving the complete two-qubit state and threshold, not implied by first-order fixed-length data. Numajiri et al. (arXiv:2510.00548) analyze whole graph fidelity under iid local Pauli noise and transfer-matrix phase transitions, and Trinh et al. (arXiv:2609.11021) analyze full-rank independent-link swapping horizons. Neither covers the parity-heralded missing-CZ double-rail crossover. The published-record and literature searches showed no directly equivalent published assertion. Possibility of an implicit or unindexed prior calculation remains.
residual_risks: The initial crazy-graph architecture and first-order susceptibility are established already in the older 2024 source; an unpublished or implicit second-order calculation may exist.
The newer 2025 and 2026 sources motivate the transfer-matrix and entanglement-horizon questions but use distinct physical noise models; their implications are not silently imported.
The critical scaling is conditional on a herald event whose probability tends to zero; no claim of a constant-rate long-range repeater is justified.
Only the specified parity-accepted protocol is assessed; alternate decoders could change the horizon.

value.rationale: The motivating graph architecture has the surprising established property of length-independent first-order infidelity under edge erasure. The new theorem identifies the exact two-error accumulation scale at which this favorable fixed-length susceptibility stops predicting successful long-distance extraction, gives a complete quantum state and a sharp operational PPT entanglement boundary, and quantifies the exponentially vanishing success probability. These facts resolve a natural noise/length tradeoff rather than a synthetic finite numerical invariant. The model is deliberately restricted to one fixed measurement protocol and is not claimed optimal.
